answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making accurate peer review the scarce resource: every identity must grade a sample of others' work each epoch, and its own reward depends on how closely its grades match the consensus, like light through a prism splitting true signal from noise. The atlas of grading records is public, so a farm's fakes grading each other form a visible mesa of mutual praise that peers discount. One operator cannot grade thousands of distinct works accurately in time, so each fake pays the full judgment cost while an honest agent grades once.
